subject.title: fix(reef): bound JSONL store file reads to prevent OOM on oversized audit/replay stores

question: For an oversized Reef replay ledger, should the runtime deny claims until the ledger is repaired, or should maintainers define a distinct verified recovery mechanism that preserves replay protection?
rationale: This is a durable replay-protection contract: silently accepting a claim after discarding later ledger records trades availability for duplicate execution, and source inspection alone cannot choose the intended security/operational policy.

options.title: Fail closed for replay state
options.body: Keep bounded partial reads for audit data if desired, but make an oversized replay ledger reject new claims until a supported repair or compaction path restores authoritative state.

options.title: Define verified ledger recovery
options.body: Specify and implement a recovery flow that preserves or reconstructs replay decisions before the gateway resumes accepting claims.

options.title: Accept prefix-only replay semantics
options.body: Deliberately allow claims missing from the retained prefix, documenting that oversized ledgers can lose replay protection.

recommendation.title: Fail closed for replay state
recommendation.body: Keep bounded partial reads for audit data if desired, but make an oversized replay ledger reject new claims until a supported repair or compaction path restores authoritative state.

likelyOwner.reason: A concrete current-main Reef protocol owner could not be established without the required local history inspection.
